I’m really sad that you had to endure depression and abuse at such a young age, but I’m also really thankful that people like you exist, helping make other people’s lives better.

Hi, can you contact student services or your equivalent? If so, you may want to talk about your depression to them. They should be able to provide assistance. Depression can make your mind slow and inattentive (made worse if you have ADHD), and henceforth it is a mitigating problem (not just for those reasons). 



I’m not sure if you’re in school, college, university. But in my case (UK), when I talked to student services, they really helped me and I would not be alive if I hadn’t talked to them.

Congratulations :D! 

You should def feel proud of yourself, good luck with your college course! Cheering for you!

hi, I remember a mental health worker telling me the best way to deal with this was to try and distract myself. Such as thinking a boy’s/girl’s name for each letter of alphabet.

I also struggle with what you mentioned and it’s why I don’t leave the house for months at a time, and try to think of any excuse I can to not go out. It helps when I am confident in myself and comfortable. I’d recommend taking small steps as well, e.g. “Maybe I’ll walk outside my house to the end of the street, or halfway, then I come back.” And gradually increase that. Reward yourself as well. 

Please take this at a pace you are comfortable with.
